title: Benchmark environment stamping and probing procedures
creator: Lena Park
description: Create a standardized playbook and lightweight tooling to 'stamp' benchmark environment artifacts and to probe target machines before running the load harness. The goal is to produce a reproducible environment fingerprint that includes driver/CUDA versions, pinned runtime image digest, kernel/driver compatibility hints, ulimit/sysctl settings, and the runner configuration used for a run. This ticket covers: 1) a small probe binary that collects deterministic host and driver information and validates GPU health; 2) a stamping format (YAML subset) that CI and local engineers can attach to benchmark runs; 3) CI validators that fail early on incompatible permutations; 4) integration with existing tokens/sec and p95 dashboards so each run links to a single stamped artifact for regression triage.
acceptance_criteria: A probe tool (linux binary + container entrypoint) produces a single stamped artifact for a host containing: kernel version, GPU driver version, CUDA toolkit version, container image digest, visible GPU topology, nvidia-smi summary, and runtime flags.
CI step that runs the probe and attaches the stamp to the benchmark job metadata in the pipeline artifacts.
Benchmark runs in nightly and PR gating reference the stamp and the dashboard links are resolvable back to the stamped artifact.
When a new run's stamp differs from the baseline in any critical field (driver/CUDA/kernel/image digest), the CI job marks the result as 'environment-delta' and surfaces a link to a comparison view.
Documentation (Confluence) describing how to interpret stamps and a troubleshooting section for common false positives (e.g., benign driver minor-version changes).
test_plan: 1) Add probe step to benchmark CI and run against two control nodes (cuda-12.3/nvidia-530 and cuda-11.8/nvidia-470) using standard seqlen profiles (short/medium/long). 2) Verify stamped artifact attaches to run and appears in the regression dashboard. 3) Run synthetic regression detection with altered driver (simulate upgrade) and ensure CI flags environment-delta and does not treat performance delta as a code regression until human review. 4) End-to-end run: stamp capture -> tokens/sec + p95 collection -> dashboard linking -> regression triage notes created.
updates: 2025-03-02: Kickoff with infra and runtime teams. Agreed probe should be read-only, low-risk, and run as non-root inside the benchmark container.
2025-03-06: Prototype probe binary created (probe-v0). Captures kernel, lsmod, nvidia-smi JSON, docker image digest. Located in GH: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-probes/pull/12.

2025-03-09: Design review with QA and CI teams. Raised trade-off: shallow vs deep probing. Decision: start shallow (nvidia-smi, driver version, cuda toolkit) and iterate; deep probing behind opt-in flag to avoid flakiness on older datacenter hosts.

2025-03-11: Added stamp schema draft to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Benchmark+Stamp+Schema. Using YAML fields: stamp_id, host_id, kernel, driver, cuda, image_digest, runner_config, timeline.
2025-03-13: CI validator prototype added to bench-pipeline. Failing case produced when image_digest changes between baseline and run. Opening follow-up to refine acceptable drift rules.

2025-03-15: Manual integration test against nightly harness completed. Stamped artifact attached and dashboard link appears in run metadata. Observed one false positive for minor driver patch; adding normalization rule to ignore micro-patch numbers in driver version by default.
notes: Trade-offs: stamping increases CI wall time by ~8-12s per job (probe run + fingerprint calculation) but reduces triage time for regression alerts. We decided to keep probes minimal to reduce false negatives caused by host-specific quirks. Future work: add a 'light' and 'deep' probe mode, and store stamps in an immutable artifact store for long-term regression forensics.
